बॉलीवुड एक्ट्रेस Shriyam Bhagnani अपनी पहली lead फिल्म Sumo Didi को लेकर सुर्खियों में हैं! 🥊

Baaghi 2 और City of Dreams 2 फेम Shriyam इस biopic में भारत की पहली महिला sumo wrestler Hetal Dave का किरदार निभा रही हैं। 🏋️‍♀️
इस रोल के लिए उन्होंने 9 महीने तक रोज 7-8 घंटे वेट ट्रेनिंग, योग, सुमो और जूडो की कड़ी ट्रेनिंग की।
Shriyam ने बताया कि फिल्म में ट्रक धकेलने से लेकर सारे stunts real हैं, इसमें कोई AI या editing का इस्तेमाल नहीं हुआ है। 🚚
रोल के लिए वजन बढ़ाने के बाद ट्रैवलिंग के दौरान लोगों ने उनसे अलग तरह से बर्ताव करना शुरू कर दिया था।
9-10 महीने का contract होने की वजह से वो दूसरा काम नहीं कर पाईं और इंडस्ट्री के लोगों ने उन्हें रिस्क न लेने की सलाह भी दी थी।

क्या आप Shriyam Bhagnani की इस जबरदस्त मेहनत को screen पर देखने के लिए उत्साहित हैं? कमेंट्स में बताएं! 👇

ctx.title: Shriyam Bhagnani recalls intense 9-month training to transform into sumo wrestler for Sumo Didi, says people treated her differently after weight gain
ctx.summary: Shriyam Bhagnani trained seven to eight hours daily for nine months to portray sumo wrestler Hetal Dave in Sumo Didi.
ctx.text:
Actor Shriyam Bhagnani took on one of the biggest challenges of her career with Sumo Didi , which marks her first film in a leading role. Having previously appeared in films such as Baaghi 2 and Aap Jaisa Koi , as well as the series City of Dreams 2, Shriyam now finds herself at the centre of a women-led sports biopic. The film follows the story of Hetal Dave, India's first female sumo wrestler, and required Shriyam to undergo an intense physical transformation to portray her on screen.
In an exclusive interview with Hindustan Times, Shriyam spoke about the nine months of training that went into preparing for the role, the challenges of playing a real-life person and the responsibility of carrying a women-led film. She also opened up about the film's long journey to its release and how her experiences in the industry have shaped her career choices.
For Shriyam, getting her first leading role in a women-led film was a big opportunity. However, the fact that it was a biopic about a real person brought with it a different kind of responsibility. She explained, "Getting a lead film is one thing, and getting a biopic, to play a real-life person, is another thing. And that too, someone who is alive and very similar to your age, so the comparison can happen very easily. So the pressure wasn't that I was leading a film; it was that her story is so powerful and unique that it needed to be done justice. There are so many sports films that have been made, but this sport is so different, and the story is so different that it needed to be told in a certain way."
Taking on the role also meant making significant changes to her physical appearance. However, Shriyam said she was not worried about being stereotyped for taking up such a role early in her career. She recalled having undergone physical transformations for other projects and how her perspective changed after seeing people's reactions to her new appearance.
A post shared by Shriyam Bhagnani (@shriyambhagnani)
Shriyam siad, "I had also gained and lost weight for other projects. Growing up, I watched actors like Aamir Khan and Johnny Depp, and I felt it was a normal process for an actor to go through this physical transformation. But once you mature, you realise that there are people who would probably not perceive you well when you are a different body type or weight. That comes in much later, and it happened after I gained the weight and the shoot had begun. When we were travelling to different places, I could see people behaving very differently with me because of that."
"I was under contract for 9-10 months and couldn't sign anything else. So if any audition was coming, I had to tell them that I couldn't take up that part and that we would take something else up. They would try to warn me, to a certain extent scare me also, saying, 'Don't give something so much time, bharosa nahi hai iss industry ka, kuch bhi ho sakta hai (You can't trust this industry; anything can happen).' And I had already changed my body type for a couple of projects that got shelved a week before filming. They were all coming from their own good places, but these things happened," she added.
Shriyam's preparation for Sumo Didi went beyond gaining weight. She underwent several hours of training every day, including weight training, yoga, physiotherapy, sumo and judo. She also stressed that the physical training seen in the film was performed by her without the use of AI or editing.
"Everything was real. There's no AI or editing. Everything you see in the film, I have done it, including pushing that truck. There were a lot of hours of training over nine months, every single day. I would say 7-8 hours of training every day, including a weight training session, a yoga session, a session with my physiotherapist, and then sumo and judo training. All of these used to happen every day.
